newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-x's Felderhof says unaware of Busang tampering.
newsitem.headline: Bre-x's Felderhof says unaware of Busang tampering.

text.p: The former exploration chief of Bre-X Minerals Ltd, John Felderhof, said on Friday he was not aware of nor did he participate in any tampering of gold samples at Bre-X's Busang deposit in Indonesia.
In a statement from his home in the Cayman Islands, Felderhof said he believed that the systems and personnel in place at Busang were adequate to detect tampering.

He also said he still believes "there is a significant amount of gold at Busang," since reports which revealed the gold fraud dealt only with the Southeast Zone of Bre-X's gold deposit, and the Central Zone "remains unchallenged."
A recent private investigation of the Bre-X debacle concluded that Michael de Guzman, Bre-X's chief geologist, salted gold samples from the Busang deposit.
De Guzman died in an apparent suicide in March this year when he fell from a helicopter in Indonesia shortly before the fraud came to light.

"I still find it very hard to believe that as a respected geologist (de Guzman) tampered with Bre-X's core samples. If Mike was involved with tampering, to my knowledge this will be the first time that a professional geologist has ever been implicated in a tampering or salting scam," Felderhof said.
He said he still believes there is gold at Busang.

"This belief is based on the structure, geology, mineralogy and alteration, as well as my many years experience in the Pacific Rim. There are still many unresolved issues to consider," Felderhoff said.
He offered several points to support his stated ignorance of the fraud, saying, "if I had known about the alleged salted or tampering with Bre-X core samples, why would I have done the following:
"I stopped selling Bre-X shares in early September 1996, in part because I believed it was undervalued in the marketplace.
"I still hold a number of Bre-X shares.
"I reinvested millions of dollars in Bre-X by converting options I held into Bre-X stock in September 1996, which stock I still hold today...
"The company hired well-known and reputable experts, such as Kilborn Engineering, Normet Pty Ltd, and Mineral Development Resources Co to review or audit our results and operations.
"We also chose well-known and reputable laboratories, such as Inchscape and Indo-Assay," Felderhof said.
He added that he also encouraged the project's partner, Freeport-McMoRan to conduct testing and due diligence.

Felderhof said throughout his time with Bre-X he urged Chief Executive David Walsh and the company's board of directors to retain the majority interest in the Busang deposit and to obtain exploration rights for all of the property surrounding the Central and Southeast zones at Busang, which he would not have done had he known of the tampering.
He also said he was not alerted to or even suspicious of tampering until after Strathcona produced its interim report.
Felderhof clarified his Busang role by saying he "was rarely in our Samarinda office and only occasionally on site at Busang."
He also countered criticism that he or other Bre-X officials should have caught the tampering because of the sampling methods used at Busang.

"My experience...suggested that crushing whole core samples was an acceptable and proper method of assaying core samples because of the spotty nature of the gold in the deposit... Therefore, if you only assay half a core you risk miscalculating the amount of gold per tonne," Felderhof said.
"It was a very simple procedure for Freeport, Strathcona, or anyone else to go back and re added.
He said there was no way to determine that the gold in the Busang samples was river gold brought in from outside and not native to the deposit.

"In my experience, and that of others, the characteristics of the gold found at Busang, some of which display gold rimmed edges and rounding, are not unusual within an oxidizing environment in the tropics," he said.

Felderhof said he was attempting to reschedule an interview with Bre-X's investigators and would continue to cooperate with regulators in Canada and the United States as the investigation of the fraud continued.
-- Reuters Toronto Bureau +416 941-8100
